rationale: Both miss the bulk of ground-truth concerns, which center on the test file (markers, skipif, try/except-masks-CI-failures) and docs (kernel version requirements) — Y ignores the test file and docs entirely, giving it lower recall than X, which at least gestures at test-rigor weaknesses and the version=1/2/default confusion. However X's headline finding (integer `version=` silently no-oping) contradicts the PR author's own explanation that version=1/2 are valid branch-version selectors, making it likely a fabricated/unverified claim presented as a confident 'Medium correctness' bug — a real precision hit on X's most prominent item. Y's four findings (narrow except ImportError, unguarded final get_kernel fallback ×2, FA2/FA3 class duplication) are all directly verifiable against the diff and delivered with precise anchored before/after snippets, giving it markedly higher precision and slightly better actionability. Net effect is a close call that favors Y for grounded correctness over X's broader but partly speculative coverage.
